what_this_is: The papers in the ACL Anthology whose title says they define a taxonomy or typology of errors, error types or quality dimensions. The frame for reading full texts, selected structurally: the pattern names no category, so a paper is here for having a scheme and not for the scheme matching ours.
why_the_title_and_not_the_abstract: The abstract pass reported its own ceiling. An abstract says it has a taxonomy far more often than it prints one, and widening its patterns filled the result with agent, SQL and retrieval papers whose errors are not properties of a text. A title is short, and a paper that defines a scheme says so there.

selection.title_says_it_has_a_scheme: \b(taxonom\w+|typolog\w+|error types?|error categor\w+|error scheme|quality dimensions?|annotation of errors?|error annotation)\b
selection.why_the_second_pattern: without it the selection fills with Universal Dependencies, FrameNet and multiword-expression schemes, which are taxonomies of language and not of error

what_the_reachability_count_measures: How much of this frame the deductive half of the layer could have found. It is a number for the bias in this review's own pipeline, not a property of the literature.
not_a_screening_decision: Nothing is included or excluded. These are papers to read, and a taxonomy is support for a criterion only once someone has read it and quoted it.
